title: test_kem.rs: ML-KEM-512/768/1024 via kem traits (PR #10305)
description:
Write tests/test_kem.rs: test ML-KEM-512/768/1024 encapsulation/decapsulation against NIST FIPS 203 ACVP deterministic vectors.

## What
Verify that ML-KEM kem trait wrappers (PR #10305) produce byte-exact shared secrets and ciphertexts matching NIST ACVP vectors.

## Design decision
kem::Encapsulate takes an opaque RNG, but NIST KAT requires deterministic encapsulation from a fixed seed.
Resolution: use the wolfCrypt C API wc_MlKemKey_Encapsulate directly (with a deterministic seed) to perform KAT testing, rather than the kem trait path.
The kem trait path is still exercised by a round-trip test (encapsulate+decapsulate agree) to prove the glue code is wired correctly.
This is documented in a comment at the top of the file explaining why direct C API usage is necessary here.

## Algorithm
1. Parse ACVP JSON from external/wychcheck/testvectors_acvp/ML-KEM-encapDecap-FIPS203/ (one JSON file per parameter set).
2. For ML-KEM-512, ML-KEM-768, ML-KEM-1024:
   a. keyGen KAT: feed 'd' and 'z' seeds to wc_MlKemKey_MakeKey; compare resulting ek (encapsulation key) and dk (decapsulation key) bytes against ACVP expected.
   b. encapDecap KAT: feed ek and m (encapsulation randomness) to wc_MlKemKey_Encapsulate; compare c (ciphertext) and k (shared secret) against ACVP expected.
   c. decap verification: feed dk and c to wc_MlKemKey_Decapsulate; compare k against ACVP expected.
3. kem trait round-trip (not a KAT — proves glue wiring):
   a. use kem::Encapsulate; let (ct, ss_enc) = mlkem512_key.encapsulate(&mut rng).unwrap();
   b. use kem::Decapsulate; let ss_dec = mlkem512_key.decapsulate(&ct).unwrap();
   c. assert_eq!(ss_enc, ss_dec);
   d. Add comment: 'This is a round-trip test only; byte-exact correctness is covered by the ACVP KAT tests above.'
4. Compile-time check: fn _kem<K: kem::Encapsulate<_,_>>() {} for each ML-KEM type.

## Defensive rules
- Document at file top that direct C API usage is intentional and restricted to test_kem.rs only
- All C FFI calls in test_kem.rs must use unsafe blocks with a comment explaining why each is safe
- Never print shared secret bytes in test failure messages (key material discipline)
- If external/wychcheck does not exist (setup.sh not run), panic with clear message

## Agent team
- Agent R: read mlkem.rs and mlkem_kem.rs (PR #10305) to find exact type names; find wc_MlKemKey_Encapsulate in wolfssl sys bindings; inspect ACVP JSON schema in wychcheck
- Agent I: write test_kem.rs per algorithm above
- Agent T: parse one ACVP ML-KEM-512 vector independently and verify it appears in the JSON file

## Tests (oracles)
- NIST FIPS 203 ACVP vectors from external/wychcheck/testvectors_acvp/ML-KEM-encapDecap-FIPS203/
- NIST FIPS 203 ACVP vectors from external/wychcheck/testvectors_acvp/ML-KEM-keyGen-FIPS203/
- PR #10305 round-trip gap explicitly documented in comments
